AltText: Aquatic plants, including water lilies, in the shallows of the Miranda River in the Pantanal at sunset. Possibly Nymphaea amazonum, whose flowers start to open at dusk.
Title: Opening time
Description:
I had photographed this patch of the Miranda River for about as long as I could tolerate the mosquitos before heading inside. Not long after, this amazing light started bathing the sky and the still water of the shallows, so I headed straight back out to this spot, where the cluster of three lily buds had been the main focus of most of my photographs. I managed to ignore the mosquitos better this time. Though I paid for it later. The species of water lily is possibly Nymphaea amazonum, whose flowers start to open at dusk. Unfortunately I have only learnt of this just now, or I would have made sure to check in on them later.

The Miranda River flows through the Cerrado before reaching the Pantanal (as in this photo). The Pantanal is the world’s largest tropical wetland, and home to an extraordinary array of plants and animals. Two of the rarest species which call this fascinating region home are the marsh deer and the giant river otter, both of which we were lucky enough to see during our stay here.
